explanation: Touching or patting someone's head, including a child's, is considered disrespectful in Singapore across all ethnic communities, since the head is viewed as the most sacred, highest part of the body. It carries extra religious weight for Malay-Muslim and Indian-Hindu Singaporeans, but general etiquette guides treat it as a no-go regardless of who you're with.
local_tip: Even an affectionate pat on a child's head can cause offense; if you want to show warmth, smile, wave, or lightly touch a shoulder instead.
regional_note: The religious weight is strongest for Malay-Muslim and Indian-Hindu Singaporeans (the head as spiritually sacred), but general etiquette guidance treats head-touching as impolite for all groups, not just these two.

also_check.note: The head is the most sacred part of the body; touching it, even a child's, is a serious offense.
The head is considered sacred, especially in Hindu tradition, and touching it without reason is disrespectful.
Patting a child's head is usually seen as a harmless, friendly gesture.

sources.title: Shoving incident in Singapore over man patting girl's head stirs heated debate - SCMP / The Vibes
